h1: The 6 Best 7-Egg Cookers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 seven-egg cookers scored on shut-off, accessories, doneness control and cleanup, all in the under $25 price bucket.
summary: The Elite Gourmet Poach and Omelet cooker is our top pick: seven boiled eggs, a two-egg poaching tray and an omelet tray, with soft, medium or hard doneness set by water. The Dash Rapid adds a chime and thermal sensor for hands-off timing. The Hamilton Beach 3-in-1 is the one if you also want a vegetable steamer. Households that only boil eggs should look at the Amazon Basics.
intro: A seven-egg cooker is a simple machine with one trick: it boils a measured cup of water and uses the steam to cook the eggs. Doneness is set by how much water you pour, not by any dial, which means the measuring cup is the most important part in the box. A cooker with a pre-marked cup and a piercing pin gets repeatable results; one with a vague cup gets rubbery yolks.

All six cookers here land in the under $25 bucket, so price will not separate them. What does is shut-off behavior, accessories, cleanup and whether a model's tray set makes it more than a boiler. We ranked them from spec sheets and listing details, scoring on how well each handles a Sunday batch of seven eggs and an everyday poached or omelet breakfast.

products.name: Elite Gourmet 7-Egg Cooker, Poach and Omelet
products.verdict: Boiled, poached and omelet from one kit, with a piercing pin built into the measuring cup.
products.description:
Elite Gourmet's 7-egg cooker boils up to seven eggs to soft, medium or hard, and the kit adds a two-egg poaching tray and an omelet tray. The measuring cup includes a piercing pin, which makes a tiny hole in the shell so steam can vent and the shell is less likely to crack.

It ranks first because it adds the most breakfast range without raising the price bucket. The Dash Rapid also includes a poaching tray and omelet bowl, but its timing relies on a thermal sensor, while here you control the water. The Hamilton Beach is close, with a steamer tray in place of a pin.

Buy it for boiled eggs plus the occasional poached breakfast. The caveat is the two-egg poaching limit, which is small for a family brunch.

products.name: Dash Rapid Egg Cooker, 7 Eggs
products.verdict: A thermal sensor shuts it off and a chime tells you, all from one switch.
products.description:
The Dash Rapid holds seven eggs and uses a thermal sensor to shut off once the water has boiled away, then sounds a chime. It includes a poaching tray and an omelette bowl, and has a single switch with no other controls.

It ranks second behind the Elite Gourmet because the chime is a convenience, not a feature that changes the food. Both cook by steam from a measured amount of water, so the audible alert is the main difference. The Dash is a better pick if you tend to wander off, and the Elite is better if you want the pin in the cup.

Choose it for set-and-forget mornings. The caveat is the single switch: there is no way to stop the cycle early beyond unplugging it.
products.idealFor: Cooks who want a clear chime and an automatic stop.
products.skipIf: You want a pin in the measuring cup or finer control.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 3-in-1 Electric Egg Cooker
products.verdict: Boils up to seven, poaches one or two, makes omelets and steams vegetables, with a beep and light.
products.description:
Hamilton Beach cooks up to seven boiled eggs, one or two poached eggs, an omelet and doubles as a vegetable steamer. A beep and an indicator light mark the end of the cycle.

It ranks third because the steamer is a bonus that many egg-cooker owners never use, while the Elite Gourmet and Dash both add more egg-specific accessories. The Hamilton Beach is the only one here that lists a vegetable steamer, which turns it into a small breakfast and side-dish steamer.

Buy it if counter space is tight and you want one gadget to do two jobs. The caveat is that poaching tops out at two eggs, and the steamer tray is shallow.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens that want a steamer and egg cooker in one.
products.skipIf: You want the most egg accessories or a piercing pin.

products.name: Amazon Basics Electric Egg Cooker, 7-Egg
products.verdict: A light 1.4 lb cooker with dishwasher-safe parts and the basics covered.
products.description:
Amazon Basics weighs 1.4 pounds, with dishwasher-safe parts, automatic shut-off, BPA-free materials and a poaching tray, egg holder and measuring cup. It is the lightest cooker listed here with a stated weight.

It ranks fourth because it offers the least extra: no omelet tray, no steamer and no chime listed. The dishwasher-safe parts do make it the easiest to clean, which counts since the heating plate and tray collect mineral scale. It beats the plain Elite Gourmet on cleanup and loses to the Dash on timing alerts.

Pick it for a small kitchen where the cooker is lifted in and out of a cupboard. The caveat is the lack of an alert, so you listen for the click instead.
products.idealFor: Small kitchens where the cooker is stored and lifted often.
products.skipIf: You want omelet or steaming extras or an audible alert.

products.name: Elite Gourmet 7-Egg Rapid Egg Cooker
products.verdict: Boil, poach and omelet at a modest feature level, with automatic shut-off.
products.description:
This Elite Gourmet Rapid cooker holds seven eggs and lists a poacher, an omelet maker, automatic shut-off and soft, medium or hard doneness. It covers the same three functions as the pricier-feeling Poach and Omelet model from the same brand.

It ranks fifth because that sibling adds a piercing pin and a clearer tray set, so you are choosing a lighter feature list over the better kit. It matches the Amazon Basics on essentials, and neither lists a chime.

Buy it if you want the three functions and do not care about the pin. The caveat is the thin listing detail, so confirm the included trays before relying on it for poaching.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want boiled plus poached or omelet options.
products.skipIf: You want the pin or a more complete tray set.

products.name: Elite Gourmet 7-Egg Electric Egg Cooker, BPA-Free
products.verdict: A BPA-free boiler with a pre-marked cup and nothing else to think about.
products.description:
This Elite Gourmet cooker boils seven eggs with automatic shut-off and a pre-marked measuring cup, in a BPA-free body. It lists no poaching or omelet trays.

It ranks last because every other cooker here adds at least one tray. The pre-marked cup is a small advantage, since marks on the cup take the guesswork out of soft, medium and hard. Against the Amazon Basics it offers fewer extras and no listed cleanup advantage.

Buy it if you boil eggs only and want the least to think about. The caveat is that poached eggs and omelets are not part of the package.
products.idealFor: Boiled-egg-only households that want the least to manage.
products.skipIf: You want poached eggs or omelets from the same machine.

whatMatters.detail: Egg cookers set doneness by the volume of water in the base, so the cup is your only control. A pre-marked cup with soft, medium and hard lines removes guesswork, and a piercing pin lets steam vent from the shell. Look for printed marks on the cup in the listing photos, and always fill to the line for the number of eggs.

When the water boils away, the heating plate heats up and a sensor or thermostat cuts power. A cooker that stops automatically prevents a dry burn-off, while a chime tells you the eggs are ready to cool. Look for the words automatic shut-off, plus a chime, beep or light if you tend to walk away mid-cycle.

Poaching and omelet trays turn a boiler into a small breakfast station, but they also add parts to wash. A two-egg poaching tray is fine for solo breakfasts and limiting for families. Check the listing for named trays and counts, and decide whether you will use them before paying for a longer feature list.

The heating plate collects mineral scale from tap water, and a crusty plate slows heating and affects results. Dishwasher-safe parts help with trays, but the plate itself needs a wipe with vinegar. Look for removable trays and a smooth plate, and plan to descale every few weeks if your water is hard.

Seven eggs sounds generous for one person and tight for a family brunch. The larger the capacity, the bigger the base, so check dimensions and weight before you buy. The Amazon Basics lists a weight of 1.4 pounds. A cooker you can stash easily will be used more often than a heavier one left in a cupboard.

faq.q: How do I get a runny yolk?
faq.a: Use less water in the measuring cup, up to the soft line. The Elite Gourmet cups are pre-marked, and the Elite Gourmet Poach and Omelet cup includes a piercing pin. Cool eggs in cold water straight away to stop cooking.

faq.q: What mistake do people make most?
faq.a: Overfilling or underfilling the cup. Water volume sets doneness, so guessing gives rubbery or raw eggs. On the Dash or Hamilton Beach, fill to the line for the number of eggs, and pierce the shell where a pin is included.

faq.q: Is an egg cooker worth it over a pot?
faq.a: If you boil eggs weekly, yes. The cooker shuts itself off, so nothing boils dry, and the Dash chimes when done. A pot costs nothing but needs a timer and watching, which an Amazon Basics or Elite Gourmet cooker removes.

faq.q: How do I poach in one?
faq.a: Add a little water to the base, place the poaching tray, crack in one or two eggs and run the cycle. The Elite Gourmet Poach and Omelet and Hamilton Beach each poach up to two eggs, so work in batches for more.

faq.q: How do I descale the plate?
faq.a: Pour a mix of white vinegar and water into the base, run a cycle or let it sit, then wipe the plate and rinse. Do this every few weeks with hard water. Dishwasher-safe trays, as on the Amazon Basics, make the rest easy.

faq.q: Can I cook fewer than seven eggs?
faq.a: Yes. Fill the water to the line for the number of eggs you are cooking, and place them evenly on the plate. All six cookers accept a partial load; the Hamilton Beach lists one to two for poached.

finalTake: Buy the Elite Gourmet Poach and Omelet cooker if you want boiled eggs plus a little more: the tray set and piercing pin make it the most flexible of six. The Dash Rapid is the pick for hands-off timing, and the Amazon Basics wins on cleanup. If you only boil, the plain Elite Gourmet BPA-free does the job at the same under $25 price.
